name: Sithri
overview: Sithri is a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified uniquely as the son of Uzziel. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional personal notes or narrative details provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Sithri may possibly mean 'YHWH is my hiding place,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew meaning. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significance through its possible connection to divine protection.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Sithri as the son of Uzziel, situating him within the Levitical lineage. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Sithri's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogy, which is important for understanding the heritage and priestly functions established by God among the Israelites. As a descendant of Uzziel, Sithri contributes to the continuity of the Levitical tribe, which was set apart for service to the Lord. Although not prominent in narrative events, his genealogical mention affirms the faithfulness of God's covenantal promises through the tribe of Levi.
